title: The dipping pair: ر ز

bigIdea.text: ر (ra) and ز (zay) share one small curve that dips below the line. No dot = 'r'. One dot above = 'z'.

proper.text: Both are a short curve that starts on the line and dips below it. ز has one dot above. Like د and ذ, they never join the letter after them. Compare: د sits on the line as a corner; ر dips below the line as a curve.

Sounds: ر is one light tap of the tongue tip just behind the upper front teeth. It is not the English 'r' with a curled tongue, and not a long roll. ز is 'z' as in 'zoo': the tongue tip stays near the front teeth with a narrow gap, so the sound buzzes and whistles.

Sifat: ر is 'in between' (tawassut: between a full stop and a full flow), it 'leans' (inhiraf), and it has 'repetition' (takrir: the tongue tip can vibrate). ز is 'soft' (rakhawa) and has a 'whistle' (safir), like ص and س.

provenance.title: صفة حرف (العربية) (Sifat of Arabic letters) — Arabic Wikipedia

proper.text: Heavy or light: ز is light. ر changes with its vowel: with a fatha or a damma it is heavy; with a kasra it is light. (A ر with sukun comes in Stage 2.)

Common mistakes. English speakers: a curled English 'r'; with a London accent, dropping ر after a vowel (as in 'car') — every ر is said. Persian/Urdu readers: ر stays light everywhere; with a fatha or damma it must be heavy. Everyone: know takrir so you can keep it small — one quick tap, not a drum roll.

points.detail: Tip of the tongue, toward its top, at the roots of the upper front teeth
Tip of the tongue with the front teeth (shared with ص and س)

memoryHook.text: Dot on top = z, no dot = r; both dip below the line.

extras.text: One light tap of ر feels like the quick 'tt' in an American 'butter'.

note.text: Starts with ر with a fatha.
Ends in ر with a shadda and a kasra.

tip.text: ر: one light tap of the tongue tip, no buzz, no whistle. ز: the tongue tip stays near the front teeth and the voice buzzes with a whistle.

questions.q: Which letter is a small dipping curve with one dot above?
explain: Right: the dipping curve with a dot is zay.
ra is the same curve with no dot.
dhal also has one dot, but it is a corner sitting on the line.
nun also has one dot above, but it is a deep bowl and joins on both sides.

questions.q: ر has a fatha. Is it heavy or light?
options: Light, because ra is always light
It depends on the next word
explain: Right: with a fatha or a damma, ra is heavy.
A kasra makes ra light, not a fatha.
ra is not always light; its vowel decides.
For a ra with its own vowel, that vowel decides.

questions.q: ر has a kasra. Is it heavy or light?
options: Heavy, because ra is always heavy
explain: Right: with a kasra, ra is light.
A fatha or damma makes ra heavy, not a kasra.
ra is not always heavy; a kasra makes it light.
A ra with a kasra is clearly pronounced.

questions.q: Which letter of this pair has a whistle (safir)?
explain: Right: zay is one of the three whistling letters (ص ز س).
ra has no whistle.
Only zay whistles.
zay does whistle.

questions.q: Which is the right way to say ر?
options: One light tap of the tongue tip behind the upper front teeth
A curled English 'r' with rounded lips
Leave it out after a vowel
explain: Right: a single, light tap.
The English 'r' is a different sound.
Keep the repetition (takrir) small: one tap.
Every ra is pronounced.

questions.q: You speak with a London accent. What is the main risk with ر?
options: Dropping it after a vowel, as in 'car'
explain: Right: many British accents drop 'r' after a vowel; in Arabic every ra is said.
ra has no whistle; that is a ز habit, not an accent habit.
ra is not a nasal letter.
Bouncing (qalqalah) belongs to ق ط ب ج د, not ra.

questions.q: How does ر differ in shape from د?
options: ر dips below the line as a curve; د sits on the line as a corner
ر has a dot; د has none
ر joins the next letter; د does not
explain: Right: curve below the line vs corner on the line.
Neither ra nor dal has a dot.
Neither ra nor dal joins the letter after it.
Their shapes are different.

options: Tip of the tongue, toward its top, at the roots of the upper front teeth
explain: Right: that is ra's point.
That is the place of ج, ش and ي.
That is the place of ع and ح.
That is the place of ب, م and و.

questions.q: Which quality belongs to ر alone?
options: Repetition (takrir): the tongue tip can vibrate
explain: Right: takrir is a quality of ra only.
The whistle belongs to ص ز س.
The bounce belongs to ق ط ب ج د.
Spreading of air belongs to ش.

questions.q: Which letters share the whistle (safir) with ز?
explain: Right: ص ز س are the three whistling letters.
dhal and ẓa are not whistling letters.
shin spreads its air (tafashshi); jim is not a whistling letter.
ra and lam 'lean' (inhiraf); they do not whistle.

provenance.title: صفة حرف (العربية) (Sifat of Arabic letters) — Arabic Wikipedia

questions.q: ر has a damma. Is it heavy or light?
options: Light at the start of a word
explain: Right: a fatha or a damma makes ra heavy.
Only a kasra makes ra light.
A ra with a damma is pronounced.
Its position in the word does not change this: the damma makes it heavy.

questions.q: Persian/Urdu readers often keep ر light everywhere. When must it be heavy?
options: When it has a fatha or a damma
Only at the start of a surah
explain: Right: fatha or damma means a heavy ra.
A kasra makes it light.
Where it sits in the surah does not decide.
ra is heavy with a fatha or a damma.

questions.q: Which pair BOTH dip below the line and never join the letter after them?
explain: Right: ra and zay.
dal and dhal never join forward either, but they sit on the line.
ba and nun join on both sides.
jim and ḥa join on both sides.

remnote: ر (ra) == No dot, dips below the line; one light tap of the tongue tip; heavy with fatha/damma, light with kasra
ز (zay) == One dot above, dips below the line; 'z' with a whistle; light
Takrir (ر) == The tongue tip can vibrate; keep it to one light tap
London-accent fix for ر == Never drop ر after a vowel; tap it every time
